title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

questions.prompt: Questioning rules and thinking about the future are examples of which type of change?
In the Johari window, things others know about you but you do not know are your…
What term describes the principles that guide a person's choices and behaviour?
Match each example to the type of change.
Suggest THREE healthy ways to cope with the changes of moving into Grade 10.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): plan and manage time; ask teachers for help; keep routines; exercise; talk to someone; join clubs; focus on what you can control

questions.prompt: Asking for honest feedback from others can increase your self-awareness.
Describe THREE strategies to build a positive self-concept.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): positive self-talk; set achievable goals; supportive friends; learn from mistakes; look after health; recognise strengths

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Relationships, Gender Roles and Power

questions.prompt: What is a gender role?
questions.memo:
✓ The behaviour, tasks and responsibilities expected of people (1)
✓ because of their gender, learned from society (1)

questions.prompt: Gender roles are learned and can change over time.
Which is NOT usually an influence on gender roles?
Which statement about consent is correct?
options: Consent can be withdrawn at any time
Being in a relationship means consent is permanent
A drunk person can give consent

questions.prompt: What is the toll-free number of the GBV Command Centre?
Name THREE warning signs of an unhealthy, controlling relationship.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): checking phone; controlling friends/movements; jealousy; constant criticism; threats; pressure for sex or images; violence

questions.prompt: Match each skill to its description.

pairs.right: Paying full attention and checking understanding
Making clear what is and is not acceptable to you

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Substance Abuse and Risky Behaviour

questions.prompt: The part of the brain that controls planning and impulse control is fully developed by age 13.
Name the South African organisation that offers treatment for alcohol and drug dependence (abbreviation).
Match each effect to the level it mainly affects.

pairs.left: Money spent on drugs instead of food

questions.prompt: Explain how alcohol use increases the risk of HIV infection.
questions.memo:
✓ Alcohol lowers inhibitions and impairs judgement (1)
✓ making unprotected sex more likely (1)
✓ and increasing the risk of sexual assault (1)

questions.prompt: Which is a protective factor against substance abuse?
What is it called when a person returns to using a substance after a period of not using it?
Give TWO ways substance abuse affects South African society.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): crime; road accidents; pressure on health services; gang activity; lost productivity; family breakdown

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Human Rights, Democracy and Discrimination

questions.prompt: Which section of the Constitution allows rights to be limited?
Freedom of expression protects hate speech.
Which institution investigates abuse of power by government officials?
Match each institution to its role.
Explain why building ramps for wheelchair users is not unfair discrimination.
questions.memo:
✓ It treats a group differently in order to give them equal access (1)
✓ so it advances equality, which the Constitution allows (1)

questions.prompt: Which rights are violated during xenophobic attacks? Name TWO.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): right to life; equality; human dignity; freedom and security of the person; property

questions.prompt: Name ONE of the three founding values on which the Bill of Rights is based.
